title: Corner case invoker issue with popover nested inside invoker doesn't account for ShadowDOM

labels.name: topic: shadow
labels.description: Relates to shadow trees (as defined in DOM)

body:
### What is the issue with the HTML Standard? https://github.com/whatwg/html/pull/10770 caught a corner case whereby buttons which point to a popovertarget that is a descendant can close the popover, if the popover is clicked (due to click event propagation). The fix was very precise: during button activation check the event target is not a shadow including descendant of the button. However I think there are two issues with this approach: 1. There is a specific issue with the current standard in that it says it should use the event's target, but that is nullable in certain cases. For example the event path crosses a shadow boundary [the target is cleared](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#dispatching-events:~:text=true%3A-,Set,event%2E). This means the following test would fail: ```html
``` If you click the button then click the popover, the expected behaviour (based on reading the spec) would be that the popover closes, but it _doesn't_ in Chrome. Looking at the Chrome source it's using a method called `RawTarget()` which says it is _not_ re-targeted (strangely the implementation looks identical to `Target()` but nevertheless Chrome passes, I think other shenanigans are going on here). So at _minimum_ I think we need to think about re-working the spec to a degree where we reference a non-adjusted target or something similar. 2. There is a meta point around all of this which is that the fix is very specific to `popovertarget`. Given we're eyeing this attribute for deprecation, given it seems a little odd to specifically fix for this. `commandfor`, for example, suffers the same issues meaning we need to apply the same fix there, to wit: ```html
``` But in addition this can be a little surprising for non-command/popover related buttons, for example it might be surprising that clicking this popover would not do what the user expects: ```html
``` So maybe there's more to do here; maybe we should consider that when a popover is clicked, it sets the default handling so that regardless of target/retargeting any interactive element ancestors are not activated?
